brief:
Slyrim is an open-world fantasy action RPG set in Hrimdal, a cold valley in the far north. The player is a courier who learns to shout with the voice of dragons and kills the old dragon Jarnorm. Every line uses a plain, technical style (ASD-STE100): short active sentences, plain words, no jokes, puns, idioms or dramatic flair. Keep that plain style in the translation. The title 'Slyrim' joins the English word 'sly' with the name of the game that inspired it; keep the title as written. The player character's body type is the player's choice; lines address the player as 'you' and never depend on gender. Use one form of 'you' for the player; people in the valley speak directly and politely. VAR, KOLT, BRASK, SKARD, ELM and HVIS are words of an invented dragon language: do not translate them.

Lines with ids starting engine. are the engine's own words: its pause menu, settings, controls screen, save slots, notices and key names. Keep them short: they sit on buttons and in narrow rows. Lines with ids starting dev. are developer text and are not translated.
